the_ruling_verbatim: i think if it cannot be reproven, then a trouble ticket. but when i say cann't be reproven i don't mean it fails and the system stops and throws an alarm. I mean if it cannot be reproven, that means something is no longer functioning correctly. so if there is a competent agent, so far limited only to you and i, it would see if it can sort the problem. might be small like an import change that got missed. then we fix it and pass it green. but if we've failed at that level, then it throws a ticket. now if it doesn't produce a bug and we merely think it might, then going back to design makes sense. still important, not URGENT. what do you think? is sending back to design too lienient?
now_the_spec_says: A sealed green whose proof cannot be reproven is red at that measurement. A competent agent attempts a bounded repair and reseals green; if repair fails, a trouble ticket; if no bug reproduces and the proof's claim is only suspect, back to design, important not urgent.
